label: b1-check-R7
text:
Node check-R7 (3 of 6): write test cases and the check of R7. The cases: at least two that break the rule, as files in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/flag, and at least two that follow it, in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/pass; each one file of what the check reads (A function or a method. Where: in the source files; read them with a parser (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_python.py, /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_js.py), or with Semgrep patterns Which files: every file that holds code, decided when the check runs (/opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md); take embedded code out of its container first (a `<script>` in HTML), then parse it), like what the agent may really write. The check: the executable /opt/enforce/checks/R7; `/opt/enforce/checks/R7 <file>` exits 0 when the file follows the rule, and otherwise exits 1 and prints each violation: R7, where (the file and line, or the part of the text), and what to change. By the route: A pattern-based static analyzer. A rule is a code pattern that Semgrep matches against each file's syntax tree, for many languages (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML script blocks, Bash, …). Check: `semgrep scan --config <rules.yml> --error --metrics=off --quiet <file>` (exit 1 on a finding; `--json` for a report) Rules: `rules: [{id: <id>, languages: [<language>], severity: ERROR, message: "<what to change>", pattern: "<code pattern>"}]`; Semgrep matches syntax, it cannot compute values (a length, a count): use a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) for those It reads A function or a method. Where: in the source files; read them with a parser (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_python.py, /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_js.py), or with Semgrep patterns Which files: every file that holds code, decided when the check runs (/opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md); take embedded code out of its container first (a `<script>` in HTML), then parse it.
Done when: /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/flag and /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/pass each hold at least two files; as the agent, the check exits 1 and names R7 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/flag, and exits 0 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/pass, and it runs semgrep. The harness checks this when you reply.
